name: Stage 41: Mellsjön to Koppartorp
description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 41, Mellsjön to Koppartorp.
utilities: Parking/access exists at Mellsjön and Koppartorp. Mellsjön-side public transport is weak, while Koppartorp/Tunabergs kyrka has the best endpoint transit but service may be limited or demand-responsive.

Koppartorp is the strong service endpoint, with seasonal summer tap, toilets, bus stop, Tunabergs kyrka, hembygdsgård, seasonal cafe/museum, Koppartorps rastplats, and mining heritage. The cafe/museum is normally a short summer-season service window, not year-round resupply.
Mellsjön shelter/toilet/tenting/fireplace/lake access is just before or near the stage start and is useful for planning, but it is primarily the stage 40 overnight node.
No shop, restaurant, or year-round potable water was verified directly along the middle of stage 41.
For year-round groceries, food, and lodging, Nävekvarn is the practical off-stage base west of Koppartorp; it is useful for linked Tunaberg/coastal hikes but not on this stage.
waterSources: Koppartorp church/hembygd summer tap is the strongest verified potable refill, but it is seasonal and should not be relied on outside summer.
No verified mid-stage potable water was found. Mellsjön and Överbosjön are natural water only; treat/filter/boil if used.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden lists stage 41 as 7 km, the 2025 long-distance pass lists 7.5 km, Naturkartan shows 7.4 km/7375 m, Äventyrligare 7.52 km, and the local app GeoJSON measures about 7.12 km. OSM relation 3822709 has correct endpoint topology but currently measures only about 5.45 km and diverges by over 1 km from the local/current line in places, so do not use OSM as the drawing source after the 2023 reroute.

Official Sörmlandsleden says a new route was completed on 2023-08-22 after landowner access changed, the old route was removed, and the first part of the text description may lag behind the updated map. Treat pre-August-2023 GPS tracks/blog distances and OSM/app-derived 5.5-6 km tracks as suspect.

Main-route topology runs from stage 40 at Mellsjön to stage 42 at Koppartorp. For route-builder stitching, snap to OSM node 2889662243 at 58.642033,16.962128 and OSM node 2889617483 at 58.645025,16.900148 while keeping the local current route geometry for drawing.
At Koppartorp the route connects to stage 42, stage 37:2, Gruvslingan/Kummelbergsrundan/Simonberget local options, and Tunabergsrundan.

Near Simonberget the route has a choice between a steeper scenic route over the top and an easier route below the southern cliff. Model this as an internal route option, not a separate stage. User reports confirm the high route is steep, rooty/rocky, exposed-feeling and rewarding; the lower route is easier but still not smooth or accessibility-grade.

Recent user reports for the wider Tunaberg/Nyköpingskusten loops warn that AllTrails and Sörmlandsleden can diverge. Follow current orange Sörmlandsleden markings and official/Naturkartan/local current geometry over old GPX/app tracks.

Simonberget/Kummelberget reserve rules are specific: tenting is allowed only below Simonberget between the dry toilet and fireplace, for at most two consecutive nights; fires only at the signed prepared fireplace; bring your own wood and do not take dead or living wood; dogs must be leashed.
Kummelberget bird-protection area is closed to access from February 1 through August 15, and climbing is forbidden there.

The stage crosses cultivated land after Överbosjön; official text says the landowner allows considerate hiking. Stay on the marked route, avoid crop damage, close gates if present, and do not rest or camp on cultivated land.

Blog and book-related reports praise the Simonberget high route as a Tunabergsrundan highlight, but note rocky ground, roots, loose stones, steep ascent, and an exposed cliff-edge feeling near the viewpoint. Hikers with knee, balance, or fitness concerns may prefer the lower/easier option.
Use current official/Sörmlandsleden/Naturkartan geometry over third-party tracks, especially because nearby Tunabergsrundan/Nävekvarn tracks can include removed or storm-damaged route segments.
Check current Nyköping/Sörmlandskusten fire-ban status before using any prepared fireplace; stricter bans can also prohibit fixed grill places.

Koppartorp/Tunabergs kyrka access is usually line 561 toward Nävekvarn with change at Buskhyttan to line 562. Line 562 service is limited, weekday-heavy in public planners, and some departures are call-controlled; verify live times and book anropsstyrd traffic when required. Current public notes for complementary traffic are date-bound, so verify 2026 service live.
The official page showed no current fault reports during the 2026-04-27 research pass.
